preamble: Debuccalization of the bilabial implosive: [ɓ] loses its labial closure and only the glottal component remains, giving [ʔ]. Proto-Mayan *bʼ, phonetically an implosive [ɓ], became ʔ at the end of polysyllabic words in Kaqchikel and Tzʼutujil (Campbell 1998: 170), while Kʼicheʼ and Mam keep it. Sobrino Gómez & Bennett describe bʼ > ʔ as a recurrent change that arose independently in several Mayan varieties (Kaqchikel, Yucatec, Tila Chol, Chontal) and attribute it to the weak oral release of [ɓ].

examples.note: The unpossessed form qʼabʼaj keeps bʼ before a suffix, the change is diachronic and lexically restricted, and bʼ still survives finally in some words (sibʼ 'smoke').

sources: Kaufman, T. (2003). A Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary. FAMSI. http://www.famsi.org/reports/01051/pmed.pdf
Campbell, L. (1998). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction. Edinburgh University Press.
Bennett, R. (2016). Mayan Phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10), 469–514. https://doi.org/10.1111/lnc3.12148
